summary: Temporary scoped prod inference-log rehydration for customer remediation — privacy controls & approval
description:
Issue summary:
Customer remediation request requires rehydration of a narrowly scoped set of production inference logs to validate and correct a small number of user-visible outputs. The customer is on a Private deployment (VPC) and their Product Ops team has requested evidence that an incorrectly applied prompt preprocessor caused token duplication for ~3 sessions on 2026-03-09.

Impact:
- Customer-facing bug prevents final approval of their release; they have paused rollouts.
- Low session volume (3 sessions, ~200 tokens each) but logs are encrypted and reside in archival blob storage.

Justification and scope:
- Exact sessions: session IDs provided by customer (redacted in ticket) — we will target these three session traces only.
- Data elements requested: timestamp, request headers (non-sensitive), model name, tokenized inputs and generated outputs; we will NOT surface full customer payload attachments.
- Purpose: reproduce the tokenization & prefix handling to confirm root cause and produce fix / remediation instructions.

Minimization & redaction plan:
- Engineering will retrieve only the specific object keys for the three session IDs.
- PII/PHI screening will run before human review using automated redaction rules (email, phone, SSN patterns).
- Any detected free-text PII will be replaced with deterministic placeholders (e.g., [REDACTED_EMAIL]).
- We will produce a minimized export containing only: session metadata, token-level input/output (token ids and position), and runtime flags. No raw attachments or customer file blobs.

Access controls & technical notes:
- Access will be performed by two engineers: one SRE and one Support Engineer. Both must authenticate via short-lived bastion creds and sign an access attestation.
- Access to the decrypted artifacts will use the ephemeral KMS key above; decryption logs will be captured in audit-logging and forwarded to security for retention.
- Export will be staged to a locked bucket with ACLs limited to the two engineers and Security reviewers; object TTL set to 24 hours then auto-delete.

Approval chain required:
- Support TL (Customer Solutions) - Aisha Kumar (reporter) — initial justification
- Security (Prod Infra) - Miguel Torres (assignee) — approve technical controls
- Privacy Officer - Sofia Patel — confirm redaction rules acceptable
- Legal (if requested) - Tara Ng — for any cross-jurisdiction exports

Deliverables and timeline:
- 2026-03-12: Security & Privacy review comments collected (this ticket).
- 2026-03-15 08:00 UTC: Access window start (pending approvals).
- 2026-03-15 20:00 UTC: Export removed per TTL and secure deletion verified.

Acceptance criteria:
- Support reproduces the issue locally with minimized artifact and documents reproduction steps in a short remediation note to customer.
- No unredacted customer PII leaves the secured staging bucket.
- All access and decryption events are logged and reviewed by Security.

Attachments: session ID list (uploaded to secure portal), initial customer remediation request email (redacted copy).
